_meta.what_this_is: A two-step next-token probability tree, the kind a language model induces over short continuations. From the start there are two first tokens: A with probability 0.55 (the local favorite) and B with 0.45. But A's continuations are mediocre (0.5, 0.5) while B's are lopsided (0.95, 0.05), so the best A-sequence totals 0.275 and the best B-sequence totals 0.4275. Greedy takes A and is stuck; beam keeps B alive and finds the more probable B-B1.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The probabilities are hand-authored so greedy's locally-best first token leads to a globally worse sequence, making the greedy/beam gap exact and checkable. Every full-sequence probability and both decoders are computed in beam.py from this tree.
_meta.format: beam_width; tree: {token: {p, next: {token: {p, next?}}}} -- each node's p is its conditional probability given the prefix; a leaf has no next.
